answerNotes.CANDLE: A candle burns fuel from its wax through a wick. Its flame produces light as the warmed wax is consumed.
answerNotes.FLAME: A flame is the visible burning region above fuel. A glowing ember is hot too, but it does not necessarily have a flame.
answerNotes.WAX: Wax can form a candle or a protective coating. A candle consumes it as fuel, while polishing leaves a thin layer on a surface.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
